To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial variability in grain size distribution is a result of the placement method and its characteristics, and that this results in a non-homogenous spatial distribution in hydraulic conductivity.

“the hydraulic conductivity in land reclamation is not spatially constant, and the degree of segregation and the resulting spatial heterogeneity of hydraulic conductivity differ between placement methods”.
land reclamations have spatially variable hydraulic conductivity because of the placement methods that were used to build the reclamations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the construction method on the hydraulic conductivity of a reclamation.
the spatial distribution of grain size and hydraulic conductivity in land reclamation constructed by bottom dumping.
the spatial variability of hydraulic conductivity in land reclamations and its implications for the recovery of freshwater from land reclamations used for aquifer storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial distribution of hydraulic conductivity is not constant, and that it should be considered as a spatially variable parameter.

the hydraulic conductivity of land reclamations can be spatially constant only if the material has been deposited by a single placement method, the grain sizes are well sorted and the material is well compacted.
the hydraulic properties in land reclamated areas are not constant and that the hydraulic properties are not only dependent on the material properties but also on the construction method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the placement method has a large influence on the hydraulic conductivity distribution and therefore should be taken into account in hydrological modelling of land reclamations.
the hydraulic conductivity of land reclamations should be considered spatially variable and not constant.
the spatial distribution of hydraulic conductivity in land reclamation can be estimated based on the placement method and its configuration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatially varying hydraulic conductivity should be applied in land reclamation models.
the hydraulic conductivity is not constant within land reclamation areas, and that this spatial variation is caused by the placement methods.
land reclamations can have spatially varying porosity and hydraulic properties and therefore should be treated as spatially variable aquifers.
